name: Yuchi
catalog_citation: Linn, Mary Sarah. 2001. A Grammar of Euchee (Yuchi). PhD dissertation, University of Kansas.
catalog_locator: Ch. 2, Sec. 5 'Stress and Intonation', Sec. 5.1 'Stress', pp. 83-86; 'Stress Pattern of Nouns' pp. 86ff; 'Stress Pattern of Verbs' p. 93
catalog_quote: Euchee has word level stress and sentence level pitch (intonation). ... Stress is the prominence of a syllable, generally by increased volume. In Euchee, a higher pitch may accompany increased volume, but high pitch is not necessary. Wagner (1934:308) stated that there is no primary position of stress in a fixed syllable of a word. While variation exists, primary and secondary stress positions can be confidently assigned. All major parts of speech (nouns, verbs, and adjectives) have primary stress on the last syllable, and secondary stress on the first syllable. This pattern is found in both inflected (those with pronominal agreement) and uninflected words. In addition, particles, one-syllable word such as location particles and the past tense, are stressed. Once this pattern is assumed, stress in Euchee is extremely regular. ... Lexical stress is distinctive in Euchee, but its function…
